proposal.description: The SS_done look-ahead on a ramp step compares the landing ceiling with the package MAX_ON_COUNTS_DEFAULT (the 'MAX_ON_COUNTS' of the port comment) instead of the programmed max_on_limit.
proposal.reason: With max_on_limit programmed below the default, the step that lands on the limit no longer raises SS_done. SS_done then rises one clock late, through the at-target branch. With the default limit nothing changes.

proposal.description: The at-target test compares the ceiling with the package default MAX_ON_COUNTS_DEFAULT instead of the programmed max_on_limit, while the clamp still loads max_on_limit.
proposal.reason: If max_on_limit is set to the floor, or lowered below a ceiling the ramp has already reached, max_on_counts keeps climbing past the limit and SS_done stays low until the ceiling reaches the default. The real design finishes at once, or clamps straight away.

proposal.description: When the ramp reaches or passes its target, the ceiling is clamped to the package MAX_ON_COUNTS_DEFAULT instead of the programmed max_on_limit.
proposal.reason: With max_on_limit below the default, max_on_counts jumps from the limit up to the default on the first S_SS clock at the target. That ceiling, above the host's limit, is then held through S_RUN.

proposal.description: The ceiling-step test compares the step-window counter with the package CYCLES_PER_STEP_DEFAULT instead of the programmed cycles_per_step, while the counter still wraps at cycles_per_step.
proposal.reason: With cycles_per_step programmed below 16, the counter wraps before it reaches 15, so max_on_counts never widens and SS_done never rises. Above 16, each step lands on the 16th cycle of its window instead of the last.
